items.title: Warren Buffett Finished Buying Coca-Cola in August 1994 and Never Bought Another Share. Under Greg Abel, Berkshire Now Collects $2.3 Million a Day From It
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway's 400 million Coca-Cola shares, bought for $1,299 million between 1988 and 1994 and never added to since, now pay $848 million a year, about $2.3 million a day. Computed from Coca-Cola's split-adjusted dividend history, the checks since 1994 add up to about $13 billion, ten times the cost, and the next $212 million payment is due December 15.

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A) Looks Fairly Valued As It Raises Yen Debt
items.summary: Why Berkshire Hathaway’s Yen Debt Sale Matters For Shareholders Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A) has raised ¥182,005 million in fresh funding through a series of yen denominated senior notes with maturities stretching from 2029 out to 2056. The new issues carry fixed coupons between 2.624% and 4.571%, are unsecured senior obligations and rank equally with Berkshire Hathaway’s other unsubordinated debt, which keeps them squarely in the mainstream of the group’s capital structure.
